title: Why do we love to dance
paragraphs: If you asked me to dance, I'd probably freeze on the spot. I lack rhythm and coordination and some people say I have two left feet! But with some persuasion and Dutch courage I can be tempted to take to the dance floor and shake some moves – and that, apparently, is only natural.

Experts have found as well as being fun, dancing might have helped us to survive as a species. Evolutionary anthropologist Bronwyn Tarr from the University of Oxford has been telling the BBC World Service CrowdScience programme that when we dance with others, we are rewarded with feel-good endorphins that change how we feel about ourselves and those around us.

Dancing alone is one thing but it's dancing as a group that makes our brain reward us with a cocktail of feel-good hormones and is likely to lead to profound social effects. It's being in sync with others that makes us happy. She says that "dancing fosters social closeness between people. It helps us build social connections and communities. In our past, those social connections would have been critical for surviving."

You certainly need the right kind of music to help you shimmy, boogie or even twerk, but once you get the right beat and get into the groove with others, it can be an uplifting experience. Even my cringeworthy dad dancing makes me feel good sometimes. And in Swindon in the UK, this 'style' of dancing has been taken to a new level, where babies, attached to their fathers' chests in a sling, have been dancing with the aim of increasing the bond between parent and child.

Dance is also a good way to keep fit and improve our mental health. In Wales there have been calls for doctors to prescribe dance classes to people who are unwell. The Arts Council of Wales claims there are many health benefits. And Bronwyn Tarr says "more and more we're actually discovering that your longevity – your life expectancy – is predicted by the social connections that you have… still today it's something we should do more of."

It could be part of being an uptight Englishman that makes me a reluctant dancer. Look at other nationalities such as Cubans where dancing is at the heart of their cultural identity. And in Brazil at Carnival time, people let their hair down by dancing together day and night. They seem to be having a good time – so maybe I should get on my feet and dance!

vocabulary.term: coordination [kəʊˌɔːdɪˈneɪʃn] n. 协调性；配合
vocabulary.entry: coordination [kəʊˌɔːdɪˈneɪʃn] n. 协调性；配合
vocabulary.example: Playing video games can actually improve coordination.
vocabulary.translation: 玩电子游戏实际上有助于提升协调性。

vocabulary.term: have two left feet [hæv tuː left fiːt] 笨手笨脚；跳舞跳得差（习语）
vocabulary.entry: have two left feet [hæv tuː left fiːt] 笨手笨脚；跳舞跳得差（习语）
vocabulary.example: He wanted to dance with her at the party, but he has two left feet—he kept stepping on her shoes.
vocabulary.translation: 他想在派对上和她跳舞，可他笨手笨脚的，老是踩到她的鞋。

vocabulary.term: Dutch courage [dʌtʃ ˈkʌrɪdʒ] 酒后壮胆；借酒壮胆（习语）
vocabulary.entry: Dutch courage [dʌtʃ ˈkʌrɪdʒ] 酒后壮胆；借酒壮胆（习语）
vocabulary.example: He only had the courage to ask her out after he had a few drinks - it was just Dutch courage.
vocabulary.translation: 他只有在喝了几杯酒后才敢约她出去——那只是酒后之勇。

vocabulary.term: take to the dance floor [teɪk tuː ðə dɑːns flɔː(r)] 走上舞池
vocabulary.entry: take to the dance floor [teɪk tuː ðə dɑːns flɔː(r)] 走上舞池
vocabulary.example: Six new celebrities are to take to the dance floor for the Christmas day special.
vocabulary.translation: 六位新晋名人将登上舞池，参与圣诞节特别节目。

vocabulary.term: shake some moves [ʃeɪk səm muːvz] 扭动身体；跳几下（口语）
vocabulary.entry: shake some moves [ʃeɪk səm muːvz] 扭动身体；跳几下（口语）
vocabulary.example: But with some persuasion, I can be tempted to take to the dance floor and shake some moves.
vocabulary.translation: 但经人稍一劝说，我就可能忍不住走上舞池扭动几下。

vocabulary.term: endorphins [enˈdɔːfɪnz] n. 内啡肽（复数，让人感到愉悦的物质）
vocabulary.entry: endorphins [enˈdɔːfɪnz] n. 内啡肽（复数，让人感到愉悦的物质）
vocabulary.example: Exercising releases endorphins that reduces your stress response.
vocabulary.translation: 运动能释放内啡肽，缓解你的压力反应。

vocabulary.term: a cocktail of [ə ˈkɒkteɪl ɒv] 多种事物的混合体
vocabulary.entry: a cocktail of [ə ˈkɒkteɪl ɒv] 多种事物的混合体
vocabulary.example: The film is a cocktail of comedy, romance and adventure.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影是喜剧、爱情与冒险元素的混合体。

vocabulary.translation: 他六岁时母亲离世，这件事对他产生了极其深远的影响。

vocabulary.term: in sync with [ɪn sɪŋk wɪð] 与……同步；与……协调
vocabulary.entry: in sync with [ɪn sɪŋk wɪð] 与……同步；与……协调

vocabulary.entry: boogie [ˈbuːɡi] v. 跳布吉舞（一种节奏明快的舞蹈）

vocabulary.translation: 我们在派对上跳着布吉舞，一直跳到午夜。

vocabulary.term: twerk [twɜːk] v. 跳扭臀舞
vocabulary.entry: twerk [twɜːk] v. 跳扭臀舞

vocabulary.translation: 她随着鼓声跳起了扭臀舞。

vocabulary.translation: 这位歌手的表演令人振奋，打动了在场的每一位观众。

vocabulary.entry: cringeworthy [ˈkrɪŋwɜːði] adj. 令人尴尬的；让人难为情的

vocabulary.translation: 他那令人尴尬的讲笑话尝试让整个房间陷入了沉默。

vocabulary.entry: sling [slɪŋ] n. 背带；吊带
vocabulary.example: The camera hung from his shoulder on a leather sling.
vocabulary.translation: 相机用皮质背带挂在他肩上。

vocabulary.term: prescribe [prɪˈskraɪb] v. 开具（药方）；建议采用
vocabulary.entry: prescribe [prɪˈskraɪb] v. 开具（药方）；建议采用
vocabulary.example: The doctor may prescribe antibiotics if the infection is bacterial.
vocabulary.translation: 若确诊是细菌感染，医生可能会开具抗生素处方。

vocabulary.entry: longevity [lɒnˈdʒevəti] n. 长寿；寿命
vocabulary.example: The study links longevity to a diet rich in vegetables and fruits.
vocabulary.translation: 该研究表明长寿与富含蔬果的饮食相关。

vocabulary.term: uptight [ˈʌptaɪt] adj. 拘谨的；紧张的
vocabulary.entry: uptight [ˈʌptaɪt] adj. 拘谨的；紧张的
vocabulary.example: He gets uptight whenever he has to give a speech.
vocabulary.translation: 他一要演讲就紧张得不行。

vocabulary.entry: let their hair down [let ðeə heə daʊn] 放松身心；不拘小节（习语）
vocabulary.example: At the company party, everyone finally let their hair down and had a great time.
vocabulary.translation: 公司派对上，大家终于放松了下来，玩得十分尽兴。
